source_text: Soleo in praescriptione aduersus haeresis: omnes de testimomio temporum compendium figere, priorem uindicans regulam nostram omni haeretica posteritate. hoc nunc probabit et apostolus dicens: de spe reposita ia caelis quam audistis in sermone ueritatis euangelii, quod peruenit ad uos sicut et in totum mundum. nam si iam tunc traditio euangelica ubique manauerat, quanto magis nunc? porro, si nostra est quae ubique manauit, magis quam omnis haeretica, nedum Antoniniani Marcionis, nostra erit apostolica. Marcionis autem cum totum impleuerit mundum, ne tunc quidem se defendere poterit de apostolica. eam enim et sic constabit esse, quae prior mundum repleuit, illius scilicet dei euangelio, qui et hoc cecinit de praedicationibus eius: in omnem terram exiit sonus eorum et in terminos orbis uerba eorum.
pass_a_gloss: I am accustomed in the prescription against heresies: all to fix a summary from the testimony of times, vindicating our prior rule against all heretical posterity. Now the apostle also will prove this, saying: concerning the hope laid up for you in heaven, which you heard in the word of truth of the gospel, which has come to you just as also into the whole world. For if already then the evangelical tradition had remained everywhere, how much more now? Furthermore, if ours is that which has remained everywhere, more than all heretical, certainly not of Antoninian Marcion, ours will be apostolic. But Marcion's, even if it had filled the whole world, not even then will it be able to defend itself as apostolic. For it will be established to be that which first filled the world, namely of that God's gospel, who also sang this about its preachings: their sound has gone out into all the earth and their words to the ends of the world.

choices.english: in the word of truth of the gospel

sound going out into all the earth

pass_b_english: In my prescription against heresies, I always nail down a summary from the testimony of the ages, vindicating our prior rule against every heretical generation. The apostle himself will now prove this, speaking of the hope laid up for you in heaven, which you heard in the word of truth, the gospel, which has come to you just as it has into the whole world (Colossians 1:5-6). If the evangelical tradition had already remained everywhere back then, how much more so now? And if ours is the one that has remained everywhere, more than any heretical teaching—certainly not that of Antoninian Marcion—then ours will be apostolic. But Marcion's teaching, even if it had filled the whole world, still could not defend itself as apostolic, not even then. For it will be proven to be the one that first filled the world, namely, the gospel of that God who also sang this about its preachings: their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world (Psalm 19:4).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that correctly identifies the scripture citations (Colossians 1:5-6 and Psalm 19:4) alluded to in the text. All clauses, including the comparison between the evangelical tradition and Marcion's, are preserved.
